title: Investigate KEDA scaler latency + HPA stabilization causing delayed scale-ups and cold-starts
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Postmortem and follow-up for a capacity regression where KEDA-triggered scaling and HPA stabilization settings combined with unexpectedly long pod init times caused user-facing tail latency and 503 errors during a traffic spike.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-09 at ~11:22 UTC a customer-facing traffic spike to hosted inference routes caused sustained queue buildup. KEDA detected the increase but metric scraping and scaler refresh intervals delayed the HPA scale-up. When new pods were created, longer-than-expected init times (model warmup + FS pulls) caused additional cold-start latency and transient 503s. Services with tight latency SLOs experienced errors for ~9 minutes until a manual capacity bump and a remediation rollout completed.
timeline: 2025-02-09 11:18 UTC - traffic increase begins; request latency rises in application metrics
2025-02-09 11:22 UTC - alert: request_5xx_rate > threshold for hosted-api-prod-route; oncall notified
2025-02-09 11:23 UTC - KEDA scaler received metric spike but scaler refreshInterval was 30s and Prometheus scrape delay pushed effective detection to ~11:24:10
2025-02-09 11:26 UTC - HPA observed desiredReplicas increase but stabilizationWindowSeconds (60s) prevented immediate scale-out beyond initial increment

2025-02-09 11:27-11:34 UTC - new pods scheduled; initContainers pull model shards and perform cold model load resulting in 8-20s pod readiness times; requests routed to ready pods where possible, but queues continued
2025-02-09 11:31 UTC - oncall applied emergency scale-up (kubectl scale) to add 8 pods, which reduced queue depth
2025-02-09 11:40 UTC - traffic returns to baseline; follow-up investigation opened (ENG-17823)
impact: Customer-facing latency and increased 5xxs across three hosted inference routes. Approx 1.8k requests failed or timed out over the incident window. No lasting data loss. A subset of high-throughput customers saw degraded throughput and increased cost due to emergency override.
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) KEDA scaler metric refreshInterval (30s) plus Prometheus scrape interval (15s) produced detection lag; (2) HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds and default scale-up policies limited quick multi-step scaling; (3) pod init path for certain models required pulling large model artifacts and performing warmup, causing long readiness delays; (4) lack of a warm-pool or predictive scaling meant we relied on reactive scale only.
detection: SRE alerting on 5xx rate and latency triggers. Internal observability dashboards (per-route queue depth, KEDA scaler latency, HPA events) surfaced the mismatch during the event. Manual investigation correlated KEDA scaler logs, HPA events, and kube-scheduler timings.
remediation: Immediate: manual scale-up to reduce queues and release traffic pressure. Short-term rollout: reduce KEDA refreshInterval from 30s to 10s for affected scalers, and lower Prometheus scrape interval for the KEDA metric endpoint to 10s. Adjust HPA behavior: decrease stabilizationWindowSeconds to 20s for critical inference deployments and enable aggressive scale-up bursts (allow 3x step in 60s) for traffic-sensitive routes. Medium-term: implement a warm-pool of pre-warmed pods for top-traffic models and add a predictive scaling prototype using rate-of-change signals. Long-term: instrument faster model artifact distribution (cache-on-node or layered downloads) and introduce a canary scaler mode for safer tuning.
action_items: AI-1: Implement KEDA scaler refreshInterval override for latency-sensitive namespaces. Owner: Luca Ramirez. Due: 2025-02-15.
AI-2: Update Prometheus scraping for keda-metrics-targets to 10s where allowed and mark in infra-scrape-policy. Owner: Mei Chen. Due: 2025-02-16.
AI-3: Adjust HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds from 60s -> 20s for inference-prod routes and create a documented policy mapping. Owner: Samir Patel. Due: 2025-02-18.
AI-4: Prototype warm-pool for top 10 models (pre-warmed pods with cached KV). Owner: Research/Infra collaboration (Priya Singh). Due: 2025-03-01.
AI-5: Reduce pod init time by implementing model artifact caching on nodes (daemon-set cache) and lazy-shard fetch. Owner: Runtime team (Diego Alvarez). Due: 2025-03-10.
AI-6: Add automated chaos/load test that simulates sudden 5x traffic spikes and validates scaler/HPA behavior. Owner: SRE Test Infra (Noah Kim). Due: 2025-02-28.
AI-7: Add alert for KEDA detection lag when metric age > 20s. Owner: Observability (Ivy Zhao). Due: 2025-02-20.
AI-8: Document emergency scale-up runbook and add RBAC task for oncall to perform controlled temporary scale increases. Owner: SRE Lead (Helena Brooks). Due: 2025-02-21.
AI-9: Post-implementation review planned after warm-pool rollout to validate cost/benefit. Owner: Product (Jared Collins). Due: 2025-03-20.
notes: Retrospective takeaway: tuning scaler and HPA parameters is a multidimensional trade-off between cost and latency; we need safer deployment patterns (canaries + metrics) and automated tests to avoid regressions.
We observed that single-parameter changes (e.g., lowering refreshInterval) can increase Prometheus load; any global change must be scoped by namespace and validated with load tests.
Follow-ups should include cross-team sign-off (SRE, Runtime, Observability) before adjusting production scaling behaviour for critical routes.
